name: ProsperoRadio
author: BlackBearReloaded
release_notes:
A new look
- The interface is rebuilt on ps5-homebrew-ui and drawn by the GPU.
- The station on air takes over the top of the home screen, with a visualizer and transport buttons; a full Now Playing view is one press away.
- A letter rail on every station list jumps to the first station under a letter, and holding L2 or R2 keeps paging.
- A Control Room for settings: volume, bass, treble, balance and mono, interface options, and the catalogue.
- Station names are drawn in every script (Arabic, Cyrillic, Chinese, Persian and more) with the console's own fonts.
- New icon and home-screen backgrounds.

Updates from inside the app
- When a newer release is listed on homebrew.page, ProsperoRadio offers to install it each time it opens: Update now, What's new (the release notes) or Skip.
- The update downloads, checks and unpacks beside the app, then ProsperoRadio closes and its files are replaced. Open it again to use the new version.
- Your favorites, settings and catalogue are kept.

Warning: Install this release as a folder: copy PPSA99001 from the ZIP to /data/homebrew/PPSA99001. If an earlier release is installed as PPSA99001.ffpfsc, remove that image. Releases no longer include an .ffpfsc image, because the app cannot update a copy installed as an image.

Under the hood
- Filesystem access comes from upstream Lapy: a resident Lapy service is used when there is one, otherwise ProsperoRadio sends its own packaged helper to the local ELF loader on port 9021. No separate payload is needed.
- Everything the app writes is in /data/prosperoradio: settings and favorites in config, the catalogue in catalog, logs in logs. Favorites from the earlier version are brought over on the first start.
- Networking moved to libcurl. Without filesystem access the app still runs, with its data in its sandbox.

Note: The first start downloads the station catalogue again, which takes about a minute.

Tested on
Two PlayStation 5 consoles: repeated launch, play and close cycles, and the update's skip, cancel, failed-check and install paths. Starting takes about three seconds longer than before while filesystem access is set up.
